en.title: At the pharmacy
en.summary: Buying medicine, understanding labels and asking a pharmacist for advice.

paragraphs: A pharmacist can advise on minor illnesses without an appointment. This lesson shows you how to describe your problem and understand the instructions on a medicine.
A customer visits a pharmacy in Cardiff with a cold.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Excuse me, do you have anything for a cold?

lines.speaker: Pharmacist
lines.text: Yes. Do you have a cough or a blocked nose?

lines.speaker: Pharmacist
lines.text: These tablets help with all three. Take one every six hours, with water.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Can I take them with food?

lines.speaker: Pharmacist
lines.text: Yes, but not with alcohol. And please don't take more than four tablets a day.

lines.speaker: Pharmacist
lines.text: They may make you feel sleepy, so don't drive after taking them.

paragraphs: **1. Instructions on medicine use the imperative.** Labels use the base verb and often a negative, with a quantity and a frequency. See Introduction to Grammar: Moods, command, subjunctive and conditional.

blocks.html:
InstructionMeaning
Take one tablet.dose
Swallow whole with water.how to take it
Do not exceed the stated dose.warning
Keep out of reach of children.safety

paragraphs: **2. Every, twice a day and once a week describe frequency.** They usually go at the end of the sentence. See Introduction to Grammar: Adverbs.

blocks.html:
PhraseExample
every six hoursTake one every six hours.
twice a dayTake it twice a day.
once a weekApply the cream once a week.
before / after mealsTake it after meals.

items: A chemist is the British word for a pharmacy; drugstore is American.
Tablets, capsules, cream and syrup are common forms of medicine.
A side effect is an unwanted result of a drug.
Over the counter means you can buy it without a prescription.

paragraphs: Pharmacists in Britain can give advice on minor illnesses without an appointment and sell many common medicines. Stronger medicines need a prescription from a doctor.
